cohort: 3,315 women from Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, and Tanzania who breastfed their last child born within two years of the survey
finding: While the prevalence of lactational mastitis in the four Sub-Saharan African countries studied was lower than in some other settings, factors such as maternal education, caesarean section, younger age, and prelacteal feeding were associated with higher odds of self-reported mastitis.
mod_finding: Women who delivered by caesarean section had 1.46 times higher odds of reporting lactational mastitis than women with a vaginal birth.
